messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: high error rate for model-warmup on cluster-15 (gpu-pool-a). Impact: ~12% request failures for /v1/serve/generate. Auto-escalation sent to Devon (on-call).

Alice N.: noticed repeated warmup failures coming out of warmup service this morning. Seeing two classes of failures: CUDA OOM during allocate, and a deserialize error reading the model blob. Occurred across 3 nodes in the pool.

Alice N.: sample logs attached below from node gpu-3: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:42Z warmup[pid=4214] ERROR model_load: failed to deserialize model: unexpected EOF while reading tensors
2026-03-15T09:12:42Z warmup[pid=4214] ERROR runtime: model load failed, error=deserialization error
2026-03-15T09:12:43Z runtime[pid=4215] WARN kernel: trying to allocate 12.3GiB but only 8.7GiB free -> cudaErrorOutOfMemory
2026-03-15T09:12:43Z runtime[pid=4215] ERROR serve: hotload failed, falling back to previous version
```

Devon (on-call): I'm on it. Joining zoom. Initial hypothesis: corrupted model artifact in the cache + aggressive prefetching causing OOM on GPUs with other resident caches. I'll triage node-level memory and artifact checksum.

Miranda (prod eng): we started a canary deploy of v2-quant last night — could the artifact layout have changed? Also seeing slightly elevated compiles at ~09:10.

Ben C.: I see repeated deserializations failing with sha mismatch on s3-sidecar during transfer. Example: `expected sha256=abc123 got=000000` for object /models/rcv1/v2/weights.pt.part. Looks like multipart upload or transient S3 read error.

SRE Rotation: I'm cordoning gpu-3 and draining warmup pods there. Marking node as under investigation in k8s: `kubectl cordon gpu-3 && kubectl drain gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Alice N.: mitigation proposal: 1) disable aggressive prefetch on warmup service for pool gpu-pool-a, 2) point warmup to fallback artifact (v2-quant-stable) for new starts, 3) restart corrupt transfer pipeline to rehydrate objects. Also notify customers if warmups delay > 30s.

Devon (on-call): implementing step 1 now. Patch: `WARMUP_PREFETCH=false` rolled out to warmup deployment in pool gpu-pool-a. Rolling restart underway.

Deploy Bot: Deployment warmup-service/gpu-pool-a updated by Devon (on-call) - rollout started.

Miranda (prod eng): also enabling an immediate fallback rule in routing for warmup failures: if warmup fails 3x in 60s, route to cold-cache path but allow requests to proceed with increased latency.

Ben C.: rehydrated the S3 part manifest for 2 artifacts. Triggered a re-upload for the broken parts. Running `aws s3 cp` integrity checks.

Devon (on-call): after rolling restart and disabling prefetch, error rate reduced from 12% -> 1.2% over 10m. A few nodes still show deserialize errors; those are being reseeded from S3.

Alice N.: customer impact assessment: affected customers on Dedicated clusters using model rcv1-v2 during the window 09:10-09:45 UTC. Estimated 140k requests, ~16k returned 5xx or timeout. We should prepare a short incident notification and contact top 5 customers with SLA windows.

Miranda (prod eng): agreed. Draft for status page: "Partial degradation for model warmup during 09:10-09:45 UTC affecting model rcv1-v2 on GPU pool A. Root cause: corrupted model object + oversubscribed prefetch behavior causing GPU OOMs. Mitigation: disabled prefetch, drained affected nodes, rehydrated artifacts, and enabled fallback routing. Full remediation: validate s3 ingest path and add checksums to warmup pipeline."

Ben C.: follow-up actions: - add multipart checksum verification in sidecar - retry logic to fail fast on corrupted parts - track S3 read exceptions in alerting

SRE Rotation: I've uncordoned gpu-4 (was drained) and re-added once rehydration complete. Leaving gpu-3 cordoned until artifact re-sync passes.

Devon (on-call): handing off to Ben C. for the deeper root cause and remediation tasks. I'm marking incident as under mitigation. Will remain available for followups. :white_check_mark:

Ben C.: taking over. I'll own the remediation and postmortem. Immediate next steps: gather full list of affected artifacts, validate s3 multipart logs (request IDs), and add canary checksum job for new uploads.

Alice N.: for the incident timeline in the postmortem, note the compile spike at 09:08 which likely increased memory pressure and coincided with the corrupted transfer window.

Incident Bot: Incident 2026-03-15-rcv1-warmup created. Severity: sev2. On-call: Devon (on-call). Owner: Ben C. Links: <https://incidents.redwood/2026-03-15-rcv1-warmup>

Miranda (prod eng): thanks everyone. Also adding a metric alert to flag deserialize errors > 1/min per pool.

Ben C.: action items assigned in the incident board. I'll post the postmortem draft in #postmortems once root cause confirmed.

Alice N.: quick note: customers on Dedicated were hit harder because their nodes had less available memory headroom due to pinned caches. We'll include recommended settings for Dedicated customers in the follow-up advisory.

Devon (on-call): closing my active paging steps. Leave the thread for remediation and comms. :thumbsup:
